prompt: Match each `WaitGroup` method with what it does to the counter.
hint: One of them does not change the counter at all.

pairs.right: raises it, runs `f` in a goroutine, lowers it after

right_distractors: sets it back to zero at once

prompt: `late.go` printed `finished when Wait returned: 0`. Why did `Wait` not wait?
hint: What was the counter when `main` reached `Wait`?

choices.text: `time.Sleep` inside the goroutines stops `Wait` from seeing them
choices.why: A sleep hides nothing from `Wait`; the counter is all it reads.

choices.text: No goroutine had run its `Add` yet, so the counter was zero
choices.why: Right. `Add` has to happen before `go`, in the goroutine that waits.

choices.text: `defer wg.Done()` ran before the work
choices.why: A deferred call runs as the function returns, after the sleep and the count.

choices.text: `atomic.Int64` is not visible to `main`
choices.why: `Load` is exactly how `main` reads it, safely; the count was 0 because nothing had finished.

prompt: What does a `WaitGroup` do when `Done` is called once more than `Add` raised it?

choices.text: It stays at zero and quietly ignores the extra call
choices.why: It does not ignore it; a counter below zero is a bug it reports.

choices.text: `Wait` waits forever
choices.why: That is what a missing `Done` does. An extra one fails loudly instead.

choices.text: It panics: `sync: negative WaitGroup counter`
choices.why: Right, with the line of the extra `Done` in the trace.

choices.text: It wraps around to a very large number
choices.why: The panic message shows the `Add` of minus one being refused, not wrapped.

prompt: A helper is declared `func fetch(url string, wg sync.WaitGroup)` and calls `defer wg.Done()`. `main` calls `wg.Add(1)` and `go fetch(u, wg)` for three URLs, then `wg.Wait()`. What happens?
hint: What does `fetch` receive: the `WaitGroup` or a copy?

choices.text: It works, since `Add` is called before each `go` statement
choices.why: The `Add` is right; the `Done` lands on a copy.

choices.text: `main` waits forever: each `Done` hits a copy
choices.why: Right. Pass `*sync.WaitGroup`, or use `wg.Go`.

choices.text: It panics with a negative counter
choices.why: Each copy starts at the value it was copied with, three or less, and goes down by one; none goes below zero.

choices.text: It does not compile
choices.why: Passing a struct by value compiles; `go vet` is what complains.

prompt: Since Go 1.25, `wg.___(f)` starts `f` as a goroutine and handles both `Add` and `Done` for it.
In `once.go`, eight goroutines called `Get` at the same moment. How many times did `load` run?

choices.text: Eight, one per caller
choices.why: That is what happens with no `Once`; the output says otherwise.

choices.text: Once
choices.why: Right: `loads: 1`.

choices.text: Between one and eight, depending on timing
choices.why: `Once` makes it one, whatever the timing.

choices.text: None, because `config` was already set
choices.why: `config` starts at its zero value; the first `Do` fills it.

prompt: What does `sync.Once` give that a boolean `loaded` checked before loading does not?
hint: What do the other callers do while the first is loading?

choices.text: It is faster than reading a boolean
choices.why: Speed is not the point; correctness is.

choices.text: The other callers wait for the load to finish
choices.why: Right. A flag says somebody started, not that the value is ready, and reading it unsynchronised is a race.

choices.text: It reloads the value whenever the file changes on disk
choices.why: It never runs the function again; `oncevalues.go` showed even an error stays.

choices.text: It retries when the function panics
choices.why: After a panic, `Do` considers the work done and does not call it again.

prompt: A service reads an API key with `sync.OnceValues` at the first request. On the day it starts, the secret store is down for a minute. What does the lesson predict?
hint: Look at the line after the file was written in `oncevalues.go`.

choices.text: The first requests fail and later ones succeed once the store is back
choices.why: That would need a retry. `OnceValues` returned the first error after the file existed.

choices.text: Every request gets the cached error
choices.why: Right. Once means once, failures included; retrying needs a lock and a flag set on success.

choices.text: The service panics at the first request
choices.why: An error is returned, not panicked; `oncevalues.go` printed it and carried on.

choices.text: `OnceValues` blocks until the store answers
choices.why: It waits only for the function to return, and the function returns the error.

prompt: Put the events of `oncevalues.go` in the order they happened.
hint: The file is written after three calls.
items: the function runs and fails to read `token.txt`
two more calls return the cached error
a fourth call still returns the error

prompt: What happened when `crash.go` wrote to an ordinary map from four goroutines?
hint: Read the first line of the output.

choices.text: Some entries were lost and it printed a smaller count
choices.why: It never reached the print; the runtime stopped it first.

choices.text: A panic that a `recover` could have caught
choices.why: It is a fatal error, which no `recover` catches.

choices.text: `fatal error: concurrent map writes`
choices.why: Right, at line 15, the assignment.

choices.text: It worked, since each goroutine used its own keys
choices.why: Disjoint keys do not make a plain map safe; the map's internals are shared.

prompt: By its own documentation, which situation is `sync.Map` optimised for?
hint: Two cases are named; one of them is here.

choices.text: Any map shared by goroutines
choices.why: The documentation says most code should use an ordinary map with its own locking.

choices.text: A map that is written much more often than read
choices.why: Heavy writes to shared keys are not one of its two cases.

choices.text: Keys written once, read many times
choices.why: Right, the first of its two cases; disjoint keys per goroutine is the second.

choices.text: A map whose `Range` must be one consistent snapshot
choices.why: Its `Range` is explicitly not a snapshot of one moment.

prompt: In `syncmap.go`, why does the program print the first visitor of `/blog` but not of `/home`?
hint: How many visits did each page have?

choices.text: `/blog` had one visit; `/home` had three, in no fixed order
choices.why: Right. Which goroutine reached `LoadOrStore` first varies by run.

choices.text: `LoadOrStore` keeps the last value for repeated keys
choices.why: It keeps the first value stored and ignores later ones.

choices.text: `sync.Map` cannot store more than one visitor
choices.why: It stores one value per key, by design here; the question is which one.

choices.text: `/home` was deleted by `Range`
choices.why: `Range` visits entries; returning `true` keeps going and deletes nothing.

prompt: `syncmap.go` recorded six visits to `/home`, `/docs` and `/blog`. What number did it print after `pages:`?
A team guards a map of user preferences, read on every request and changed by any request, with `sync.Map` 'because it is the concurrent one'. What does the lesson say to prefer?
hint: Is the access pattern one of the two cases?

choices.text: `sync.Map`, since it has the locking inside
choices.why: Having the locking inside is not enough; the access pattern is neither of its two cases.

choices.text: An ordinary map with a `Mutex`
choices.why: Right: typed, simpler, and an `RWMutex` only if measurement shows readers waiting.

choices.text: An ordinary map with no lock, as writes are short
choices.why: `crash.go` is what that becomes: a fatal error.

choices.text: One `sync.Once` per key
choices.why: Preferences change; `Once` would freeze the first value for ever.

prompt: Which of these are mistakes `go vet` or the runtime reported in this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: One was `go vet`, two were the runtime.

choices.text: `WaitGroup.Add` called from inside the new goroutine
choices.why: Yes, `go vet` on `late.go`.

choices.text: A negative `WaitGroup` counter
choices.why: Yes, a panic in `negative.go`.

choices.text: Concurrent writes to an ordinary map
choices.why: Yes, a fatal error in `crash.go`.

choices.text: An error cached by `OnceValues`
choices.why: That is the documented behaviour, and nothing reports it.
